statement: A rideshare driver keeps $75\%$ of every fare she collects, and she pays $\$18$ per day to rent her car. Her fares average $\$12$ each. What is the least number of rides she must give in one day so that she keeps at least $\$150$ after paying the rental?

choices.misconception: I forgot that she keeps only $75\%$ of each fare, so I solved $12n - 18 \ge 150$ and got $n \ge 14$.
I left out the $\$18$ rental, so I solved $9n \ge 150$, got $n \ge 16.7$, and rounded up to $17$.
I solved $9n - 18 \ge 150$ correctly to get $n \ge 18.7$ but rounded down to $18$, which leaves her with only $\$144$.

hints: How much does she keep from one $\$12$ fare?
She keeps $0.75 \cdot 12 = 9$ dollars per ride. Write an inequality for what she keeps after the rental, solve it, then round sensibly.

solutions.reliable: She keeps $0.75 \cdot 12 = 9$ dollars per ride. After $n$ rides and the rental she has $9n - 18$ dollars. We need $9n - 18 \ge 150$, so $9n \ge 168$ and $n \ge 18.\overline{6}$. Rides come in whole numbers, so she needs $19$. Check: $18$ rides leave $162 - 18 = 144$ dollars, too little, while $19$ rides leave $171 - 18 = 153$ dollars.
